clue.text: Animal has big antlers upfront, in a bearskin

indicators.note: in says those initials are put inside the hat

parts.note: a busby is a tall fur hat worn by guardsmen, which is what a bearskin is

indicators.note: upfront asks for the front letter of each of the three words before it

explanation.surface: A creature with huge antlers is somehow wearing a guardsman's tall fur hat.
explanation.walkthrough: 'upfront' signals the initials of the three words; 'in' puts them inside the guardsman's fur hat, splitting it. A busby is the tall fur cap of British guards regiments.
explanation.definitionFit: A galago, the small big-eyed African primate, is commonly called by this name, so it is an example of an animal.

clue.text: Serial killer, miserable beast, died

parts.note: feeling blue is feeling miserable
a bear is a beast

explanation.surface: A tabloid description of a murderer as a wretched beast who has now died.
explanation.definitionFit: The folktale nobleman murdered wife after wife, so his name stands for a serial killer.

clue.text: Plant -—- a specimen's about to freeze up

indicators.note: up in a down clue means the whole is read from bottom to top
about means wrapped around the frozen word

parts.note: one is a specimen, as in 'here is one'; with the 's it is ONES
ice is frozen water, so freeze gives ice

explanation.surface: A plant specimen is about to freeze up in the cold.
explanation.walkthrough: 'about' wraps the specimen word round the frozen water, giving OICENES; 'up' then turns it, as this is a down clue.
explanation.definitionFit: Groundsel and ragwort belong to this large genus, so it is a plant.

clue.text: Lead the school, and wield the axe

definitions.meaning: to be the principal, the teacher in charge of a school
to chop off someone's head with an axe

explanation.definitionFit: Split in two the word means to serve as headteacher; whole, it means to decapitate with a blade.

clue.text: Tip from Cook keeps woman quiet

indicators.note: keeps means holding the woman word inside

parts.note: to bake is to cook
she stands for a woman
sh is the call for quiet

explanation.surface: A tip from a cook that keeps a woman quiet.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Tip' looks like advice but is the gratuity; 'from' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: A Persian-derived word for alms or a gratuity given in the Middle East and India, so a tip.

clue.text: Got home so easily and played with energy

definitions.meaning: a horse that won a race with great ease is said to have done this home
children frolicking boisterously have done this

explanation.definitionFit: The verb covers both winning comfortably, as in racing slang, and playing in a lively, boisterous way.

clue.text: Capital once run through by eccentric economist

indicators.note: run through means pierced, so the eccentric is inside the city

parts.note: Rio de Janeiro was once the capital of Brazil
a card is an eccentric or comic character

explanation.surface: An old capital city overrun by an eccentric economist.
explanation.walkthrough: 'eccentric' looks like an adjective for the economist but is the noun 'card'.
explanation.definitionFit: David Ricardo was the classical British economist of comparative advantage, a named example of an economist.

clue.text: At last, pick me up during bank holiday and delight me

indicators.note: during means put within the holiday

parts.note: May Day, 1 May, is a British public or bank holiday

indicators.note: At last asks for the final letter of the word pick
up in a down clue reads the word me from bottom to top

explanation.surface: Someone asks to be collected on a bank holiday, which would delight them.
explanation.walkthrough: 'At last' gives K and 'up' turns the first 'me' over; 'during' places KEM within the holiday after its second letter. May Day is a British public holiday.
explanation.definitionFit: The Clint Eastwood catchphrase is an idiom inviting something that would please the speaker, so it means delight me.

clue.text: City hospital built over one of the most beautiful fields

parts.note: Ely is a cathedral city in Cambridgeshire

indicators.note: built over means the hospital is constructed around the one

parts.note: san is short for sanatorium, a hospital
one is the Roman numeral I

explanation.surface: A city hospital is built on one of the loveliest fields.
explanation.walkthrough: Ely is a small English cathedral city. 'built over' wraps SAN round I.
explanation.definitionFit: In myth the Elysian Fields were the paradise of the blessed, so the word describes the most beautiful fields.

clue.text: Make, say, pot

indicators.note: say signals that the word for make is spoken, giving a word of the same sound

parts.note: to make money is to earn it

explanation.surface: A potter is told to make, for example, a pot.
explanation.walkthrough: 'say' looks like 'for example' but marks a sound-alike: EARN, said aloud in a British accent, matches the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: A large vase or vessel, often for ashes or for tea, is a kind of pot.

clue.text: There's nothing vital to come after each tap dance

parts.note: the two taps on a basin are marked H for hot and C for cold
nothing is zero, the letter O
vital means key, as in a key player
the second tap is the cold one, marked C
nothing again gives O
vital again gives KEY

explanation.surface: A grim remark that there is nothing important left after each dripping tap.
explanation.walkthrough: The phrase 'nothing vital' (O KEY) is placed after each of the two taps, H and C.
explanation.definitionFit: A party song-and-dance in which people put limbs in and out and shake them about; it is a group dance.

clue.text: Pain has returned — one's out of hospital

parts.note: someone who has returned is back

indicators.note: out of means the card word is on the outside, wrapped round the hospital letter

parts.note: an ace is a one in cards; the 's is short for is
H is the abbreviation for hospital on maps and signs

explanation.surface: A patient's pain comes back just as they are discharged from hospital.
explanation.walkthrough: 'one's out of hospital' reads as a discharge but means ACE (one) is outside H, making ACHE; 'one's' is 'one is'.
explanation.definitionFit: An ache in the lumbar region is a specific kind of pain.

clue.text: May I interrupt soldier attached to regiment? Continue!

indicators.note: attached to puts the soldier joined on to the regiment, with the regiment first

parts.note: RE, the Royal Engineers, is the regiment

indicators.note: interrupt says the I breaks into the soldier word

parts.note: a soldier is a man, as in officers and men

explanation.surface: A soldier politely asks permission to interrupt before being told by his regiment to carry on.
explanation.walkthrough: 'May' is just part of the polite request. RE is the Royal Engineers, a British Army corps.
explanation.definitionFit: To stay on or carry on existing is a synonym of continuing.

clue.text: What sex is this cat? It's tiny

definitions.meaning: male cats are toms, so the reply is the indefinite article plus that word
the smallest particle of an element is a very small thing

explanation.definitionFit: The basic particle of matter is the byword for something minute, and split as two words it names a male cat.

clue.text: Hear teacher at her desk teach badly

indicators.note: Hear says the phrase is spoken, giving a word of the same sound

parts.note: a female teacher is called Miss, and at her desk she is in the form room, a form being a class

explanation.surface: A command to listen to the teacher at her desk who teaches badly.
explanation.walkthrough: A school form is a class; the teacher, Miss, is in her form.
explanation.definitionFit: To give someone wrong information is to teach them badly, a near synonym.

clue.text: Feel bad about arresting mere defendant

indicators.note: arresting means holding, so the lake word is caught inside

parts.note: to feel bad about something is to resent it
a mere is a lake or pond

explanation.surface: Someone feels guilty about having a mere defendant arrested.
explanation.walkthrough: 'mere' looks like 'only' but is the noun for a small lake.
explanation.definitionFit: In a divorce or appeal case, the party who answers the petition is the defending party, the legal synonym.

clue.text: The end for Brutus with cold, angry speech

parts.note: Brutus was defeated and killed himself at the battle of Philippi in 42 BC

explanation.surface: Brutus meets his end with a cold and an angry speech.
explanation.walkthrough: Brutus, Caesar's assassin, died after losing the battle of Philippi.
explanation.definitionFit: Named after Demosthenes's attacks on Philip of Macedon, it is a bitter denunciation, an angry speech.

clue.text: Bland column suppressed by news agency

indicators.note: suppressed by means held inside the agency name

parts.note: TASS was the Soviet news agency
a stele is an upright stone slab or pillar

explanation.surface: A dull newspaper column is censored by a news agency.
explanation.walkthrough: 'column' reads as a newspaper column but is a stone pillar.
explanation.definitionFit: Food lacking flavour is flavourless, so bland and flat in taste.

clue.text: Simple garland: girl on bike takes part of it

parts.note: Daisy is the girl in the old song 'Daisy, Daisy' riding a bicycle made for two
the chain is a part of a bicycle

explanation.surface: A girl cycling along picks up part of a flower garland.
explanation.walkthrough: The music-hall song 'Daisy Bell' has Daisy on a 'bicycle built for two'; 'it' is the bike.
explanation.definitionFit: Children link the stalks of small white flowers into a loop, the simplest kind of floral garland.

clue.text: Level area in a French port

indicators.note: in means the area letter is placed inside the port

parts.note: Brest is a port in Brittany

explanation.surface: A flat area in a port in France.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Level' reads as flat ground but means side by side.
explanation.definitionFit: Two runners alongside each other are level, side by side, which is the sense here.

clue.text: Have a burn-up and cause a scene across motorway

indicators.note: across means stretched over, so the fuss word encloses the motorway

parts.note: to create is to make a fuss, cause a scene

explanation.surface: A joyrider has a race on the motorway and causes a scene.
explanation.walkthrough: A 'burn-up' is slang for a fast drive, but here it is a literal burning.
explanation.definitionFit: To dispose of a body by burning is to give it a burn-up, a playful phrase for incineration.

clue.text: Disease is not mine, I may tell you

indicators.note: telling someone means speaking, so the word is given by its sound

parts.note: what is not mine is yours

explanation.surface: Someone insists the illness is not theirs, as they may tell you.
explanation.walkthrough: In a non-rhotic British accent YOURS sounds the same as the disease name.
explanation.definitionFit: A tropical infection of the skin, bones and joints caused by a bacterium; it is a disease.

clue.text: Boil has burst, so getting wipe out

indicators.note: burst means broken apart, so these letters are scattered and reassembled

explanation.surface: A boil has burst, so it is getting wiped clean.
explanation.walkthrough: 'burst' rearranges BOIL and HAS together.
explanation.definitionFit: To do away with a law or practice altogether is to eradicate it, to wipe out.

clue.text: Surrender hypodermic in the end — where did it go?

indicators.note: in the end asks for the last letter of the word hypodermic

parts.note: a syringe needle goes into a blood vessel, so the reply is the article plus vein

explanation.surface: Someone asks where the hypodermic went, before surrendering at the end.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in the end' gives C; the question 'where did it go?' is answered 'a vein'.
explanation.definitionFit: To give in or collapse under pressure is a phrasal synonym of surrender.

clue.text: In charge, new Machiavellian ruler

indicators.note: In says the new letter goes inside the charge word

parts.note: the charge for something is its price

explanation.surface: A new ruler, in charge, behaves in a scheming Machiavellian way.
explanation.walkthrough: 'In charge' looks like a phrase meaning 'in command', but 'In' is the container signal and 'charge' is the fee.
explanation.definitionFit: Machiavelli's famous treatise on ruthless statecraft is titled after a sovereign ruler, the one it advises.

clue.text: Answer for obtaining berth in long ship

indicators.note: obtaining a berth in something means getting a place inside it

parts.note: to long for something is to pine

explanation.surface: Someone answers that they are after a berth on a long ship.
explanation.walkthrough: HMS Pinafore is the ship of Gilbert and Sullivan's comic opera.
explanation.definitionFit: The title vessel of the Gilbert and Sullivan operetta is a named example of a ship.

clue.text: Lose papacy after trashing sacred book

indicators.note: after trashing means the letters have been wrecked and rebuilt in another order

explanation.surface: Someone loses the papacy after trashing a holy book.
explanation.walkthrough: 'after trashing' looks like a time sequence but is the anagram signal on the two words before it.
explanation.definitionFit: The Book of Revelation, the last book of the Bible, goes by this Greek name, so it is a sacred book.

clue.text: Conflagration giving off first heat

indicators.note: giving off means losing, here the first letter is lost

parts.note: a conflagration is a fire

explanation.surface: A blaze gives off heat first of all.
explanation.walkthrough: 'heat' looks like the temperature of the fire, but means anger.
explanation.definitionFit: Heat in the sense of passion or rage is a synonym of anger.

clue.text: A painful thing one may have to face, including road obstruction

indicators.note: including means holding the road inside the swelling word

parts.words: A painful thing one may have to face
parts.note: a stye is a sore swelling on the eyelid, so on one's face
the M1 is Britain's main north-south motorway, written MI in crosswords

explanation.walkthrough: 'one may have to face' reads as 'confront', but the stye is literally on the face. The M1 is England's London-to-Leeds motorway.

clue.text: A religious reformer suppresses hypocrisy, getting decoration

indicators.note: suppresses means holding down, so in the answer the reformer comes after the hypocrisy

parts.note: cant is hypocritical, pious talk
Jan Hus was the Czech religious reformer burnt in 1415

explanation.surface: A church reformer stamps out hypocrisy and is given an honour.
explanation.walkthrough: 'suppresses' means keeping down, so the reformer comes beneath, i.e. after, the hypocrisy. Jan Hus was a Bohemian forerunner of the Reformation.
explanation.definitionFit: The spiny leaf of this Mediterranean plant was carved on Corinthian capitals as an ornament, a classic architectural decoration.
